title: Malaysia Police Recruitment 2026: PDRM Requirements Guide
metaDescription: Malaysia police recruitment 2026 guide: PDRM constable and inspector requirements, SPM qualifications, height and fitness standards, training and how to apply.
headline: Malaysia Police Recruitment 2026: How to Join PDRM

sections.title: What is PDRM recruitment?
sections.content:
The Royal Malaysia Police, known as PDRM, is Malaysia's national and federal police force. It recruits constables, inspectors and officers through public intakes, with education, physical fitness, medical health and vetting all checked before training begins.

A constable normally needs at least SPM, the Malaysian Certificate of Education, while inspector routes usually need a diploma or higher qualification. Applicants must be Malaysian citizens and pass written, fitness and interview stages.

sections.title: Physical and medical standards
sections.content:
Published PDRM standards list a minimum height of 163 cm for men and 157 cm for women for inspector, sergeant and constable posts, without shoes. Men also face a chest measurement of 81 cm normally and 86 cm on inhalation, plus minimum weight rules.

Candidates must pass a vision test, normally V/6/9, and must not be colour blind. A government medical officer must certify fitness, and hearing, general health and body mass are also considered during the medical stage.

sections.title: Training at PULAPOL
sections.content:
Selected constables undergo about six months of training at a Police Training Centre, known as PULAPOL, while inspectors train for about nine months. Training covers Malaysian law, police science, weapons handling, drill, physical training and martial arts.

The course is designed to build discipline, fitness and professional conduct. Recruits who fail fitness, academic or conduct standards during training may not graduate, so preparation before joining matters as much as the application itself.

sections.title: How to apply and prepare
sections.content:
Applications are normally made through the official government recruitment portal when an intake opens, so candidates should watch official PDRM announcements rather than relying on social media posts. Keep SPM results, identity documents and certificates ready before applying.

Prepare with regular running, bodyweight exercise and revision of Malay language, general knowledge and basic law. Honest answers in vetting and interviews matter, because background checks form a central part of police recruitment.

faqs.q: What qualification is needed to join PDRM as a constable?
faqs.a: A constable normally needs at least SPM, the Malaysian Certificate of Education. Inspector routes usually require a diploma, while higher officer routes may need a degree. Exact academic conditions depend on the post advertised, so always check the official intake notice for that vacancy.

faqs.q: What are the height requirements for Malaysia police?
faqs.a: For inspector, sergeant and constable posts, published standards require at least 163 cm for men and 157 cm for women, measured without shoes. Men must also meet a chest standard of 81 cm normally and 86 cm on inhalation, plus minimum weight and vision requirements.

Constables normally train for about six months at a Police Training Centre (PULAPOL), while inspectors train for about nine months. Training includes Malaysian law, police science, weapons handling, drill, physical fitness and martial arts, with discipline and conduct assessed throughout.

faqs.q: Who can apply for PDRM recruitment?
faqs.a: Applicants must normally be Malaysian citizens who meet the age, education, physical and medical standards for the post. They must pass written tests, fitness screening, a medical examination, interviews and vetting. Criminal history, health and fitness can all affect the final decision.
